messages.subject: Creating interaction variable with var1:var2?
parts:
Dear all,

I am trying to perform a moderated mediation model in lavaan, but I seem to have trouble getting the interaction factor in the model.

My model code is this:

 

model3.2 <- ' # direct effect

             SecurityCC ~ c1*AAI_2forcedCC

           # mediator

             Sens_centr ~ a1*AAI_2forcedCC

             SecurityCC ~ b1*Sens_centr

           # Moderator

             SecurityCC ~ c2*NE_centr

             SecurityCC ~ b2*Sens_centr:NE_centr

             SecurityCC ~ c3*AAI_2forcedCC:NE_centr

         '

fit <- sem(model3.2, data = data_sens_temp, missing = "pairwise", ordered = c("SecurityCC"), link="probit")

summary(fit)

 

SecurityCC and AAI_2forcedCC are factor variables (binary), Sens_centr and NE_centr are continuous variables.

 

When I run this model, I get an error saying that some variables have no values (only missings). When I look in the specifications, I can see that this is the case for the interaction variables ‘Sens_centr:NE_centr’ and ‘AAI_2forcedCC:NE_centr’. I don’t understand why this is not working, because I thought the ‘:’ is used to create an interaction term. I do prefer to have the interaction made in the model, because I intend to run the same model in a set of imputed datasets. Can anyone give me some advice on this?

 

Thanks so much in advance!

Marije

I don’t understand why this is not working, because I thought the ‘:’ is used to create an interaction term.

It does, but I'm not sure how that feature works with pairwise deletion.  Try simply adding the product terms to your data set and including those variables explicitly in the syntax, so you don't need the colon operator.

Terrence D. Jorgensen

messages.subject: Re: Creating interaction variable with var1:var2?
parts:
Marije,

I haven't used mitml, but as a general recommendation for this situation:

* Include the product term in the imputation frame (present when both components are non-missing, missing otherwise)
* Do not impute the product term. Alternatively, discard the product term from the imputed dataset
* Compute the product term in the imputed datasets from the components, just in regular data management syntax

Then analyze.

Pat
